name: K2 (Godwin-Austen / Chhogori)
terrain: Steep mixed granite pyramid, technical ice gullies (House's Chimney, Black Pyramid, Bottleneck hanging serac).
summary: Earth's second-highest and undisputed most dangerous technical mountain. Known as 'The Savage Mountain' that tries to kill you, K2 offers zero easy walking routes to its summit.

name: Nanga Parbat (Diamir / The Killer Mountain)
terrain: Features the Rupal Face, the biggest sheer mountain wall on planet Earth rising 4,600m vertically from base.
summary: The western terminus of the Himalayan chain. Renowned for its sheer scale, volatile weather, avalanche-prone couloirs, and Hermann Buhl's legendary solo summit push on Pervitin.

name: Broad Peak (K3)
terrain: Long summit crest over 1.5km long above 8,000m; scree lower slopes yielding to steep snow couloirs and razor ridge.
summary: Situated directly across the Godwin-Austen glacier from K2. Historically climbed in pure lightweight alpine style by Hermann Buhl's team in 1957 without porters or supplemental oxygen.

name: Gasherbrum I (Hidden Peak / K5)
terrain: Remote southeastern corner of the Baltoro basin; intricate icefalls and complex avalanche-swept couloirs.
summary: 'Gasherbrum' translates from Balti as 'Beautiful Mountain'. Site of Messner & Habeler's seminal 1975 pure alpine-style ascent of an 8,000m peak.

name: Mount Everest (Sagarmatha / Chomolungma)
terrain: Khumbu Icefall labyrinth, Western Cwm, Lhotse Face blue ice, South Col gale winds, Hillary Step ridge.
summary: The highest pinnacle of Earth. Climbed primarily via the Southeast Ridge from Nepal or the North Ridge from Tibet.

name: Mont Blanc (Monte Bianco)
terrain: Grand Couloir rockfall hazard, Gouter ridge scramble, Bosses knife-edge snow ridge, high summit snow dome.
summary: The monarch of Western Europe, offering high-altitude glacial terrain easily accessible from the world-class climbing center of Chamonix.

name: The Matterhorn (Monte Cervino)
terrain: Exposed Class 4-5 rock slabs on the Hornli Ridge, fixed hemp/wire ropes on the Shoulder, summit snow roof.
summary: The world's most dramatic pyramidal rock horn. Demands precise footwork in crampons over mixed rock and ice with thousands of meters of vertical drop.

name: Great Trango Tower
difficulty: World Class Big Wall (Grade VI, 5.11+ A4)
terrain: The greatest vertical drop on Earth: over 1,000 meters of sheer, near-vertical granite monolith rising from the Baltoro glacier.
expeditionType: Capsule Big Wall Aid & Free Climbing
summary: The ultimate big wall climbing test in the world. Requires portaledge camping hanging in mid-air over thousands of feet of exposure.

name: Rakaposhi (Mother of the Mist)
terrain: Unbroken rise of nearly 6,000 meters from the Hunza riverbed to the summit in just 11 kilometers horizontal distance.
summary: One of the most visually dominant and sheer mountains on Earth when viewed directly from the Karakoram Highway near Karimabad.

name: Monte Fitz Roy (Cerro Chaltén)
difficulty: World Class Technical Rock & Ice (Grade V-VI)
terrain: Polished vertical granite towers constantly assaulted by Roaring Forties winds, rime ice mushrooms, and sudden blizzards.
summary: The crown of Patagonia. Famous for tiny weather windows requiring climbers to sprint up 1,000 vertical meters of granite within 24-36 hours.
